question: A work permit identifies ___________ and ___________ to mitigate the hazards.
explanation: A work permit identifies specific risks and the corresponding controls required to mitigate workplace hazards[cite: 17].

question: When isolating an electric motor driven pump, you should first:

options.A: Close the high pressure steam inlet valve

explanation: Electrical isolation (opening the motor breaker/switch) is the primary first step before isolating process fluids when working on motor-driven equipment[cite: 17].

question: The duties and responsibilities of the Workplace Health and Safety Committee is described in:
explanation: The roles, duties, and responsibilities of workplace health and safety committees are formally outlined under labor legislation such as the Canadian Labour Code[cite: 17].

question: Sour Gas (gas containing H2S) has a distinct smell of "rotten eggs" in low concentrations. Quality training and safe work practices are required to avoid:
explanation: Hydrogen sulfide is extremely toxic and can quickly paralyze the olfactory nerve at higher concentrations, making proper safety training critical to prevent fatal exposure[cite: 17].

question: Ensuring the work area has been cleaned up is found in which part of a work permit:
explanation: Final housekeeping, equipment restoration, and area clean-up sign-offs are standard components of the permit completion and closure stage[cite: 17].

question: TDG acts and regulations require training and certification for:

options.A: Workers who ship or receive dangerous goods
options.B: Workers who ship or receive non-hazardous or hazardous products
options.C: Only for the supervisors of employees handling hazardous items
options.D: Only for people who transport Dangerous goods
options.E: Only for federal government employers and employees

explanation: Transportation of Dangerous Goods (TDG) regulations mandate formal training for anyone handling, offering for transport, shipping, or receiving dangerous goods[cite: 17].

question: When a lockout requires modification, the operator follows:
explanation: Complex lockout procedures are instituted when dealing with multi-source energies or situations requiring modifications to standard isolations[cite: 17].

question: In a safety lockout, all ________ that cause harm or damage must be controlled.
explanation: The fundamental goal of a safety lockout is to isolate and control all forms of hazardous stored or potential energy[cite: 17].

question: Emergency evacuation drills should be carried out:
explanation: Regulatory standards generally require emergency evacuation drills to be conducted at least annually to ensure staff readiness[cite: 17].

question: Under federal jurisdiction, a workplace health and safety committee must be established when the number of employees is:
explanation: Federal labor regulations mandate a workplace health and safety committee for work locations with 20 or more employees[cite: 17].

question: The 2 types of lockouts are:
explanation: Safety lockouts are broadly categorized into personal lockouts and group lockout systems[cite: 17].

question: A first aid attendant is required when there are:

options.A: Only workers are doing manual labour
options.B: Only during day shift when supervisors are present
options.E: 6 site workers, but supervisors and managers are not counted

explanation: Occupational health and safety rules stipulate that a designated first aid attendant must be present when employee counts reach specified thresholds, such as 6 or more workers[cite: 17].

question: A bump test is performed:

options.A: At the local on/off hand switch
options.B: Only after the steam pressure is reduced to zero
options.C: At the main breaker in the MCC

explanation: A bump test is performed on electrical breakers or motor controls to verify that the correct equipment has been de-energized before opening or working on it[cite: 17].

question: Fall protection must be used when a worker is at risk of falling:
explanation: General safety regulations require fall protection systems whenever workers are exposed to a potential fall height of 2 meters or more[cite: 17].

question: Emergency response plans include:
explanation: Comprehensive emergency response plans encompass evacuation routes, muster stations, equipment locations, and designated personnel training[cite: 17].

question: Requirements for entry into confined spaces are governed by the:
explanation: Confined space entry protocols and safety standards are mandated under occupational health and safety regulations[cite: 17].

question: Confined space means any enclosed or partially enclosed space having:

options.A: Limited room for tools and equipment
options.B: Harmful gases, vapours, mists, or dusts

explanation: A confined space is legally defined by having restricted means of entry and exit along with limited natural ventilation[cite: 17].

question: Asbestos is dangerous when it is:
explanation: Asbestos fibers become a severe health hazard when friable fibers are disturbed and inhaled into the lungs[cite: 17].

question: Group lockbox lockout procedures requires at least 2 people:
explanation: Complex group lockbox systems typically involve distinct roles such as an installer who applies isolations and a verifier who confirms zero energy state[cite: 17].

question: Hydrogen Sulphide, H2S, is commonly found in:
explanation: Hydrogen sulfide is encountered across oil and gas extraction, wastewater treatment facilities, mining operations, and petroleum refineries[cite: 17].

question: Using a non intrinsically safe camera in a natural gas area would require:
explanation: Electrical devices that are not intrinsically safe can produce sparks and require a hot work permit when operated in potential explosive gas atmospheres[cite: 17].

question: The flash point of a liquid is the temperature which:

options.B: It will form a gas and burn

explanation: The flash point is the minimum temperature at which a liquid gives off enough vapor to form an ignitable mixture with air[cite: 19].

question: Under WHMIS rules, what must an employer do?

options.B: Train workers about the hazardous materials on the worksite
options.D: Provide MSDS sheets to their customers

explanation: Employers have a legal obligation under WHMIS to provide comprehensive education and training regarding hazardous products present in the workplace[cite: 19].

question: The ignition temperature of an air/fuel mixture is the:

options.A: Temperature at which the mixture is above the boiling point
options.B: Maximum temperature before the fuel turns to vapor
options.C: Temperature at which it is said to have lean mixture
options.D: Temperature at which the fuel will gel
options.E: Lowest temperature at which it will burn

explanation: Ignition (or auto-ignition) temperature is the lowest temperature required to initiate self-sustained combustion in an air-fuel mixture without an external spark[cite: 19].

question: The purpose of WHMIS is:

options.A: Provide suppliers with a method to avoid liability
options.B: Provide a legal framework for OH & S enforcement
options.C: Provide workers with information to safely use hazardous materials
options.D: Provide management with information to purchase hazardous materials
options.E: Provide hazardous material information to homeowners

explanation: WHMIS is designed to ensure workers are provided adequate health and safety information regarding hazardous materials through labels, SDSs, and training[cite: 19].

question: When pouring or transferring hydrocarbon solvents used for cleaning:

options.B: Training is not required for this task
options.C: Only maintenance staff do this work
options.D: It is not allowed to transfer from the supplier containers to smaller ones

explanation: Handling volatile solvents requires appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) and engineering controls to mitigate chemical and vapor exposure[cite: 19].

question: All gas cylinders must be kept:
explanation: Compressed gas cylinders must be securely chained and stored in an upright position to prevent tipping and valve damage[cite: 19].

question: Which WHMIS document contains the most comprehensive information?
explanation: The Safety Data Sheet (SDS) provides detailed technical, toxicological, and handling data exceeding what is found on product labels[cite: 19].

question: In order for hydrocarbons to burn, the:

options.B: Air/fuel mixture should be above the upper flammable limit
options.C: Temperature must be below the boiling point

explanation: Liquid hydrocarbons must first vaporize into gaseous form in order to mix with oxygen and undergo combustion[cite: 19].

question: Acetylene and Oxygen cylinders should be stored:
explanation: Compressed oxygen and fuel gas cylinders (like acetylene) must be stored safely apart—typically at least 6 meters—or separated by a fire-rated barrier[cite: 19].

question: Proper storage for lubricating oils and grease is:

options.B: In a flammable material storage cabinet
options.E: All of these answers are correct

explanation: Lubricants should ideally be kept in their original sealed supplier containers to prevent contamination and degradation[cite: 19].

question: For WHMIS, the employer must:

options.B: Verify that employees have been successfully trained
options.C: Use substances that are non hazardous

explanation: Employers are responsible for ensuring that workers receive effective instruction and training and verifying their understanding[cite: 19].

question: The workplace label is completed at the worksite:

options.A: Is identical to the supplier label
options.B: Only when stored inside a building
options.C: Is not required at an outside jobsite
options.D: If the supplier label is damaged

explanation: A workplace label must be applied when a hazardous product is decanted into a secondary container or when the original supplier label becomes unreadable or damaged[cite: 19].

question: The Safety Data Sheet (SDS or MSDS) is supplied by the:
explanation: Chemical manufacturers and suppliers are legally required to provide Safety Data Sheets for controlled products[cite: 19].

question: If a supplier label is not on a product that comes to the worksite:

options.A: The supervisor can write up a temporary one
options.B: It cannot be used until one is supplied
options.C: Workers can attach the MSDS to the product and continue to use it
options.D: A workplace label can be used instead
options.E: Supplier labels are not really required

explanation: If a product arrives missing a supplier label, a compliant workplace label must be created and affixed before use[cite: 19].

question: When receiving gas cylinders, you should inspect them for:

options.A: Damage due to nicks or scrapes

explanation: Incoming cylinders must undergo thorough pre-check inspections covering physical structural damage, correct identification labels, and pressure status[cite: 19].

question:
WHMIS contains 4 basic components:
a. Employee training
b. Hazard Identification and classification
c. Confidentiality of information
d. Supplier and workplace labels
e. Material safety data sheets
explanation: The core operational elements of WHMIS include hazard classification, labeling, safety data sheets, and worker training[cite: 19].

question: What is the purpose of the inert, slightly pressurized blanket gas on a tank?

options.A: To ensure air does not get into the tank
options.B: To make the fuel mixture lean
options.C: To provide additional head for the transfer pump
options.E: To prevent corrosion in the tank

explanation: An inert gas blanket maintains slight positive pressure to prevent air and moisture ingress, thereby eliminating flammable vapor mixtures and tank corrosion[cite: 19].

question: If the fuel amount is below the lower flammable limit, the mixture:

options.A: Must have a source of ignition

explanation: An air-fuel mixture with insufficient fuel concentration (below the lower flammable limit) is too lean to support combustion[cite: 19].

question: The duties of a power engineer responsible for loading, unloading, pumping, transferring hydrocarbon liquids includes the regular monitoring of:
explanation: Safe transfer and storage operations require constant monitoring of levels, pressures, temperatures, tank bottom water draws, and vapor spaces[cite: 19].

question: To prevent Class C fire, electrical equipment should be approved by:
explanation: Electrical installations and equipment must bear certification marks from recognized testing authorities like CSA or ULC to ensure safety against electrical fires[cite: 20].

question: The major advantage of CO2 as a fire extinguishing agent for fires in electrical equipment is that it:

options.A: Has superior cooling ability over other agents
options.B: Provides a barrier between oxygen and burning materials
options.E: Does not reduce the oxygen content of the area

explanation: Carbon dioxide dissipates completely without leaving conductive or chemical residues that could ruin sensitive electrical switchgear[cite: 20].

question: Which of these should be avoided when using or maintaining oxygen equipment?
explanation: Pure oxygen reacts violently with hydrocarbons; oils and grease must never be used to lubricate oxygen valves or regulators due to explosion hazards[cite: 20].

question: A reducing agent or fuel could be:
explanation: Carbon monoxide acts as a fuel/reducing agent because it can undergo further oxidation in a combustion reaction[cite: 20].

question: Burning Sodium may be extinguished by using:
explanation: Class D fires involving reactive combustible metals like sodium require specialized dry powder extinguishing agents[cite: 20].

question: A Class B fire is extinguished by:

options.B: Lowering the temperature of the burning liquid
options.C: Wetting the burning paper or wood
options.D: Creating a chain reaction between the molecules of the materials
options.E: Lowering the temperature of the burning wood or paper

explanation: Class B fires involving flammable liquids are best controlled by blanketing or smothering to cut off oxygen[cite: 20].

question: The best type of fire extinguisher to use on an electrical fire would be a:
explanation: Carbon dioxide units are ideal for electrical fires because they are non-conductive and leave no damaging residue[cite: 20].

question:
For combustion to occur, the following four criteria must be met:
a. Must be able to continue
b. Must be fuel to burn
c. Must be pressurized
d. Oxygen is present
e. Ignition source available
explanation: Sustained combustion requires fuel, oxygen, an ignition source, and a self-sustaining chemical chain reaction (the fire tetrahedron)[cite: 20].

question: Work that creates a source of ignition is:
explanation: Any maintenance or construction task involving welding, cutting, grinding, or open flames is classified as hot work[cite: 20].

question: Fire - rated (FR) clothing should be worn:

options.A: Only when working directly with an open flame
options.C: At all times everywhere in the work place
options.E: When there is a possible exposure to an ignition source

explanation: FR apparel is required whenever workers face potential flash fires or arc flash hazards in industrial facilities[cite: 20].

question:
A fire can be stopped by:
a. Removing or cutting off the fuel supply
b. Cooling the material below the ignition temperature
c. Removing or cutting off the oxygen supply
d. Installing an effective fire detection system
explanation: Fires are extinguished by removing any element of the fire triangle: cutting fuel, cooling temperature, or smothering oxygen[cite: 20].

question: An effective method to identify potential fire hazards and reduce the chances of fire is:
explanation: Performing systematic fire risk assessments helps identify vulnerabilities and mitigate potential ignition scenarios[cite: 20].

question: In addition to automatic fire detection systems, what additional fire monitoring is required?

options.B: Regular reports to Human Resources department
options.E: Regular reporting to the federal government

explanation: Routine physical plant inspections and operator rounds serve as a vital manual check alongside automated fire detection loops[cite: 20].

question: To prevent fire when storing combustible metals:

options.A: The metal should be hermetically sealed and immersed in oil
options.B: No special precautions are required as long as it is in a metal cabinet
options.C: The cabinet should be oxygen free
options.D: A water based fire extinguisher should be near by
options.E: Signage should be in place to indicate what is being stored and what can't be stored with it

explanation: Alkali and reactive metals like sodium or potassium react violently with moisture and air, requiring immersion in mineral oil or hermetic sealing[cite: 20].

question: A class A fire would involve:
explanation: Class A fires involve ordinary combustible solids such as wood, paper, coal, cloth, and rubber[cite: 20].

question: A class K fire occurs with:
explanation: Class K fires involve combustible cooking media such as animal fats, vegetable oils, and deep fryer greases[cite: 20].

question: To extinguish a fire, aqueous film forming foam agents act in order to:
explanation: AFFF (Aqueous Film-Forming Foam) acts by cooling the fuel surface, forming a vapor barrier to seal out oxygen, and smothering the flames[cite: 20].

question: Class A fires are extinguished by:

options.E: None of these answer are correct

explanation: Water and water-based extinguishers primarily extinguish Class A fires by soaking and cooling the burning material below its ignition point[cite: 20].

question: When ignition can occur without any apparent external ignition source:
explanation: Spontaneous combustion occurs when a material reaches its auto-ignition temperature through internal chemical or biological heating without an external spark[cite: 20].

question: Halon agents are:

options.A: Safe until they make contact with combustion process
options.C: The best extinguishers for Class K fires
options.E: Able to maintain cylinder pressure regardless of temperatures

explanation: Halon clean agents displace oxygen and produce thermal decomposition byproducts that can be toxic in confined spaces[cite: 20].

question: The gaseous products of combustion are toxic and can:

options.B: Have immediate and long term health effects
options.C: Have only short term health effects
options.D: Have only long term health effects
options.E: Are not a concern when you are in fresh air

explanation: Inhaling smoke and combustion gases can cause acute asphyxiation as well as chronic long-term respiratory damage[cite: 20].

question: Power engineers who are familiar will all areas of their plants should provide input to the fire risk assessment, including:

options.B: Evaluate the possibility of a fire starting
options.C: Evaluate the severity of impact from a fire
options.D: Developing steps to prevent a fire starting
options.E: All of these answers are correct

explanation: Plant operators contribute essential operational insights to fire risk assessments by identifying hazards, calculating impact, and formulating prevention controls[cite: 20].

question: The following is a class B fire:

options.A: An oil fire on the surface of a flare pit
options.B: A fire in a coal bunker
options.D: A fire in an electrical panel
options.E: A fire in a wood pile

explanation: Flammable liquid pool fires, such as oil on a flare pit surface, fall under Class B fire classifications[cite: 20].

question: The best fire extinguisher to use on a hydrocarbon fire would be:
explanation: AFFF (Aqueous Film-Forming Foam) is exceptionally effective on hydrocarbon fuel spills because it floats and seals the liquid surface[cite: 20].

question: Regular cleaning is an effective way to prevent which type of fire?
explanation: Good housekeeping practices—such as removing dust, paper scrap, and trash—prevent the accumulation of Class A fuel sources[cite: 20].

question: Water is the best extinguisher for:
explanation: Water is the standard and most effective extinguishing medium for solid wood and cellulose fires[cite: 20].

question: To minimize the panic that people experience in a fire situation, most companies:

options.A: Use military style command structures to control employees
options.B: Employ psychologists to train workers to not panic
options.D: Only hire people who never panic

explanation: Regularly scheduled fire drills build familiarity and calm, structured responses during actual emergencies[cite: 20].

question: Your first reaction to a fire should be to:

options.B: Get to the nearest fire extinguisher

explanation: Life safety always takes absolute priority; personnel must ensure people are evacuated from immediate danger before attempting fire suppression[cite: 20].

question: Which of the following is a class C fire:

options.A: A fire in a wood pile
options.B: A fire in an electrical panel
options.C: An oil fire in a fuel tank
options.D: A fire in a coal bunker

explanation: Class C fires specifically involve energized electrical equipment[cite: 20].

question: Foam extinguishers are recommended for:
explanation: Standard foam extinguishers are rated for Class A (solid combustibles) and Class B (flammable liquids) fires[cite: 20].

question: Good practices to prevent fires from getting started include:

options.B: Keeping flammable materials distributed throughout the site
options.C: Storing combustible materials next to sources of ignition
options.E: Allowing heat sources to contact only Class A fuel sources

explanation: Enforcing strict smoking prohibitions in industrial areas eliminates a major common ignition source[cite: 20].

question: The best portable fire extinguisher to use on a class d fire is the:
explanation: Dry powder extinguishers are specifically formulated to smother and quench combustible metal fires without reacting dangerously[cite: 20].

question: Identifying and repairing leaks in equipment is a good way to prevent:
explanation: Fixing process leaks prevents flammable liquid or gas accumulations that fuel Class B fires[cite: 20].

question: Halon extinguishers:
explanation: Halon and clean agents chemically interrupt the combustion chain reaction rather than just cooling or smothering[cite: 20].

question: The best type of fire extinguisher to use on deep fat fryer would be a:
explanation: Wet chemical extinguishers saponify hot cooking oils, creating a cooling soapy foam blanket that seals Class K fryer fires[cite: 20].

question: Material transferred by hoses can be a source of ignition due to:
explanation: Flowing non-conductive hydrocarbons through hoses generates electrostatic charge buildup, requiring proper bonding and grounding[cite: 20].

question: Which of these state the requirements for fire detection and suppression systems?

options.C: National Fire Code, National Building Code

explanation: Building design, fire detection, and active suppression systems are governed by the National Fire Code and National Building Code[cite: 20].

question: You should check your standpipe and sprinkler systems to ensure there is no restriction to access:

options.B: It is the fire department's responsibility

explanation: Routine weekly inspections ensure that fire protection equipment, control valves, and standpipe connections remain unobstructed and accessible[cite: 21].

question: Which is the most common sprinkler system?
explanation: Wet pipe sprinkler systems—which keep water permanently charged right up to the sprinkler heads—are the most widely installed type[cite: 21].

question: The most basic instruction to remember for using a handheld fire extinguisher is PASS:
explanation: The acronym PASS stands for Pull the pin, Aim at the base, Squeeze the handle, and Sweep side to side[cite: 21].

question: One type of extinguisher that is suitable for all five classes of fire is the:

options.E: None of these is suitable for all types of fire

explanation: No single portable fire extinguisher agent is universally rated and suitable for all five distinct fire classes without specific limitations[cite: 21].

question: For flammable liquid fires, foam type extinguishers can achieve best results by:

options.A: Lobbing the foam over top the fire
options.B: Bouncing the foam off the floor just in front of the burning area
options.C: Splashing the agent into the burning pool
options.D: Discharging the agent with a sweeping movement
options.E: Discharging the agent at the base of the pool

explanation: Deflecting foam off a nearby vertical surface or floor allows it to gently sweep across a liquid fire without submerging and splashing the burning fuel[cite: 21].

question: The responsibility to inspect and maintain fire extinguishers is:
explanation: Facility owners and management bear ultimate legal responsibility for ensuring fire extinguishers are regularly inspected and maintained[cite: 21].

question: Checks that should be done when the pump is not running includes:

options.D: Verify that the inlet and outlet valves are locked open

explanation: Stationary fire pump readiness checks include confirming that critical suction and discharge isolation valves are fully open and secured[cite: 21].

question: To ensure the engine, engine oil, coolant, bearings are all running well at operating temperatures the fire pump tests usually last for at least:
explanation: Routine operational testing of diesel-driven fire pumps typically runs for at least one hour to reach stable thermal equilibrium[cite: 21].

question: You should check the fire pump engine oil level:

options.B: The fire department checks oil levels
options.E: Only when there is a noisy bearing

explanation: Engine fluid levels, including crankcase oil, must be checked and verified before starting the fire pump engine[cite: 21].

question: The standpipe system that contains water, but is not hooked up to a permanent water supply is:
explanation: A manual wet standpipe contains water for hose connection but lacks an automatic water supply pump, relying on fire department pumper trucks to supply pressure[cite: 21].

question: To prevent accidental discharge, fire extinguishers are usually:

options.B: They are kept in locked cabinets

explanation: Handheld extinguishers feature a safety ring pin secured through the operating handle to prevent accidental actuation[cite: 21].

question: An advantage of the Halotron I extinguisher is:

options.A: It is non corrosive, environmentally acceptable

explanation: Halotron I clean agents offer non-corrosive, non-conductive suppression with improved environmental profiles compared to older halons[cite: 21].

question: Gas turbine engine enclosures use CO2 to fill the cabinet:

options.C: To set off the fire detection system
options.E: To provide less oxygen to the engine

explanation: Total-flood carbon dioxide systems inject CO2 into gas turbine enclosures to rapidly displace oxygen and smother internal fires[cite: 21].

question: Hydrostatic testing of sprinklers and standpipes should be done:

options.E: None of these answers is correct

explanation: High-pressure hydrostatic testing of fire protection piping is performed on extended multi-year schedules rather than daily, weekly, or monthly[cite: 21].

question: Which type of sprinkler system has heads that are not heat activated and always fully open?
explanation: Deluge systems utilize open sprinkler heads across the entire protected zone, flooding the area simultaneously when a fire detection loop trips[cite: 21].

question: Portable fire extinguishers are grouped by this type of operation:
explanation: Portable fire extinguishers are categorized based on their mechanical expelling action (such as stored pressure, cartridge-operated, or pump tank)[cite: 21].

question: Sprinkler systems in computer rooms and telecommunications facilities typically install:
explanation: Pre-action sprinkler systems prevent accidental water release in sensitive IT rooms by requiring both detection alarms and sprinkler link fusion before water enters the pipes[cite: 21].

question: All maintenance work done on portable fire extinguishers is required to be:

options.B: Supervised by a National Fire Protection Association employee
options.C: Completed in all extinguishers in the plant at the same time
options.E: Performed at the work site in case they are required in an emergency

explanation: Servicing, recharging, and internal inspections of fire extinguishers must be executed by certified fire protection service agencies[cite: 21].

question: A major disadvantage of a floor standing pump extinguisher over a packpack unit is:

options.A: The floor unit is too difficult to move
options.B: The packpack unit has twice the range
options.C: The floor unit has only half the capacity
options.E: The floor unit pump is single acting

explanation: Floor-standing pump tanks require the operator to stop pumping and physically move the canister when relocating, unlike wearable backpack units[cite: 21].

question: The stored pressure extinguisher is charged with pressure up to:
explanation: Standard stored-pressure dry chemical extinguishers typically operate at internal charge pressures around 900 kPa[cite: 21].

question: Fire pumps are usually started automatically when:

options.B: The pressure in the system drops
options.C: When the fire alarm is sounded

explanation: Fire pumps feature automatic pressure switches that start the main fire pump when system pressure drops due to sprinkler activation or hose deployment[cite: 21].

question: The type of extinguisher that requires an Air Aspirating nozzle:
explanation: Aqueous film-forming foam (AFFF) extinguishers require specialized air-aspirating nozzles to entrain air and properly generate the foam blanket[cite: 21].

question: During inspection, an acceptable way to determine if the extinguisher is full is:

options.B: Ensure it is easy to access
options.E: Check the hoses are in good condition

explanation: Weighing portable extinguishers during routine inspections verifies that the contents have not leaked or discharged over time[cite: 21].

question: Jockey pumps are sized to have:

options.A: Enough capacity to fight small fires
options.B: Enough flow to circulate the whole fire standpipe system
options.C: Enough power to prevent pipeline freezing
options.D: Enough capacity to pressurize the standpipe
options.E: Enough pressure to reach 3 story fires

explanation: A jockey pump is a small auxiliary pump designed solely to maintain normal holding pressure in fire protection piping against minor leakage[cite: 21].

question: Standpipe systems are used in buildings over three stories because:

options.A: Fourteen meters is the limit for dragging fire hoses up the stairwells
options.B: Fire hoses can only spray water up three stories
options.C: Fire trucks can't reach over three stories
options.D: Fire hoses are only fourteen meters long
options.E: All of these answers are correct

explanation: Standpipes provide pre-connected water connections in stairwells because height limits (approx. 14 meters) make dragging lengthy loose hoses from ground vehicles impractical[cite: 21].

question: The use, occupancy, and construction of a building determines:

options.A: The class of the standpipe system used
options.B: The size of hose and hose connections to be used
options.C: The number of fire zones for standpipes
options.D: The number and location of standpipes
options.E: Frequency of maintenance by the fire department

explanation: Building codes use occupancy type, size, and construction class to dictate standpipe quantities and strategic positioning[cite: 21].

question: When the conditions might result in freezing temperatures, the preferred sprinkler system is:
explanation: Dry pipe sprinkler systems keep piping filled with pressurized air rather than water until a sprinkler head opens, preventing freezing in unheated areas[cite: 21].

question: Carbon Dioxide (CO2) extinguishers:

options.A: Are the best for Class A fires
options.E: Are the most difficult to use

explanation: Carbon dioxide extinguishers are self-expelling because CO2 is stored under high pressure as a liquefied gas that discharges on its own[cite: 21].
